RANDOM CHECKS: Per TSA guidelines, Amtrak conducts random ticket/ID verification checks onboard, so be prepared to show valid photo ID to onboard crew upon request.

BUYING TICKETS ONBOARD: Passengers purchasing tickets onboard from a conductor must show photo ID and be at least 16 years old (a service fee applies and cannot be waived); passengers boarding at staffed stations/kiosks should buy tickets before boarding.

BAGGAGE: All baggage should have an ID tag (free tags available at stations).

CANADA TRAVEL: If crossing the US-Canadian border, additional border crossing requirements apply (see Amtrak's separate Border Crossing Information page).

answer.answer:
Found on Amtrak's 'Passenger Identification' page (https://www.amtrak.com/planning-booking/tickets-id-safety-security/passenger-identification), reached via Amtrak.com > PLAN tab > 'Passenger ID, Safety & Security' > 'Passenger Identification'. Key information: 

1) VALID PHOTO ID REQUIRED: Amtrak customers 18 years of age and older must produce valid photo identification when: exchanging/refunding/reprinting Amtrak travel documents; purchasing documents with a stored eVoucher or Transportation Credit; traveling as a Pass Rider (active or retired); storing baggage at stations; checking baggage (including firearms); sending Amtrak Express shipments; asked onboard trains by train crew or other Amtrak/railroad employees; asked any time by Amtrak police or any law enforcement officer; traveling into Canada; or a guardian purchasing an unaccompanied minor's travel documents/signing the release form.

2) WHAT COUNTS AS VALID ID (for ages 18+): identification must be current and in force, and you need either (a) one piece of photo ID issued by a government authority, OR (b) two pieces of ID, at least one issued by a government authority. Acceptable examples: state or provincial driver's license; passport; official government-issued ID (federal, state, city, county, or foreign government); Canadian provincial health card ID with photo; military photo ID; student ID (university, college, or high school photo ID); Job Corps photo ID.

3) RANDOM TICKET/ID CHECKS: Following TSA guidelines, Amtrak conducts random ticket verification checks onboard, so passengers should be prepared to show valid photo ID to onboard crew upon request.

4) PURCHASING TICKETS ONBOARD: Passengers buying tickets onboard from conductors must show photo ID and be at least 16 years old (a service fee applies and cannot be waived); passengers at staffed stations or stations with a kiosk should buy tickets before boarding.

5) BAGGAGE: All baggage should have an ID tag (free tags available at stations); baggage restrictions apply (see Amtrak's baggage policy page).

6) US-CANADA BORDER TRAVEL: If your trip crosses the US-Canadian border (train or Amtrak Connection bus), review Amtrak's separate border crossing information page, as additional documentation (e.g., passport) requirements apply. No sign-in, booking, or personal data entry was needed to find this information.
